plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $39. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, bidding my exact value maximizes potential profit. By bidding $39, I ensure I only win if the item is truly worth more to me than other bidders, and I'll pay less than my valuation if I win. This strategy minimizes the risk of overbidding and potential losses.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly at my private value ($20) is the dominant strategy. This prevents overpaying if I win and ensures I maximize potential profit. Since values are independently redrawn each round, past strategies are irrelevant. By bidding my true value, I minimize the risk of either overbidding (losing money) or underbidding (potentially losing the auction unnecessarily).

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly my private value ($20) is the dominant strategy. This eliminates the risk of overbidding and ensures I won't pay more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independently drawn each round, strategic learning from past rounds isn't applicable. My goal is to maximize potential profit by bidding truthfully and avoiding unnecessary losses.
